root_cause_label: Agent launched QEMU with no plan to automate the interactive Windows XP installer and immediately pivoted to nginx configuration, never completing the installation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent launched the QEMU VM with the XP ISO but had no strategy to drive the interactive installer (e.g., unattended answer file or VNC keystroke automation), then immediately abandoned the installation task to thrash on nginx restart failures for the rest of the trajectory.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: Agent runs 'qemu-system-i386 -m 512 -hda /app/isos/xp.img -cdrom /app/isos/xp.iso -boot d -vnc :1 &' and considers the VM launch complete, but has no mechanism to automate the interactive Windows XP setup wizard — no unattended winnt.sif, no VNC keystroke scripting, no expect/xdotool plan — making successful installation impossible from this point.
t_commit_evidence: Step 8: After a brief VNC check (step 7, which returned empty output), the agent pivots entirely to nginx ('which nginx'), framing the web interface as the next major task. From this point the agent never returns to the Windows XP installation process, locking in failure.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge that launching QEMU with an interactive installer ISO requires additional automation (unattended setup file, VNC keyboard scripting, or similar) to complete the installation without human interaction at the console. It proceeded as if booting from the ISO would self-install Windows XP.
forewarning_evidence: Step 7: netstat for port 5901 returns '(command not found in terminal output)' — no confirmation — yet the agent in step 8 claims 'I've confirmed that the VNC server is running on port 5901', indicating the agent misread an empty result as success and then shifted away from the installation problem entirely.
